mainTopic: How the משמרות share offerings and the לחם הפנים around the רגלים, and the order of the ברכות of סוכה and זמן
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא about the רגלים, when all the משמרות serve together in the בית המקדש. From ״חלק כחלק יאכלו״ it learns that they all share the לחם הפנים equally. From ״לבד ממכריו על האבות״ it learns that offerings not connected to the רגל stay with the משמר whose week it is. The גמרא then discusses whether, on the first night of סוכות, the ברכה of סוכה comes before or after זמן (שהחיינו). רב says סוכה first because the obligation of the day comes first. רבה בר בר חנה says זמן first because the more frequent ברכה comes first. The גמרא tries to link this dispute to בית שמאי and בית הלל on קידוש, but rejects the link. It then answers a challenge to רב from the שבועות bread distribution. The הלכה follows רב: סוכה, then זמן. Next the גמרא explains which extra offerings the scheduled משמר brings on the רגל. Finally, a new משנה teaches how the twelve loaves of לחם הפנים are divided between משמרות when יום טוב is near שבת and during the rest of the year, and how משמר בילגה was penalized.

steps.title: All shifts share the eating equally
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses ״חלק כחלק יאכלו״ to show that on a רגל all the משמרות share the eating equally, just as they share the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'They shall eat portion like portion.' Just as they share equally in the service, so they share equally in the eating.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about the רגלים. It brings a פסוק to prove that every priestly shift gets an equal share of the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a רגל, all the משמרות serve together in the בית המקדש. The phrase ״חלק כחלק״ ties the eating to the service. If everyone shares the work equally, everyone shares the food equally.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
Portion like portion, meaning equal shares
Eating, here meaning the priests' share of holy food

phrases.english: The verse states:
'They shall eat portion like portion,'
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק in דברים יח:ח.

phrases.english: just like the portion of service, so is the portion of eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a רגל, all משמרות share the eating equally, just as they share the service.

steps.title: Which eating does the verse mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which food the ״אכילה״ of the פסוק refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what 'eating' is this talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a clarifying question: which food is the ברייתא talking about? This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the shifts share 'the eating' equally, but it never said which food. The גמרא wants to pin down the exact case.

phrases.english: And what eating is meant?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the term אכילה in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which food is being shared equally among the משמרות.

steps.title: It cannot mean offerings, since that is already known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the verse means קרבנות, because another פסוק already teaches that the priest who offers a קרבן shares in eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means offerings, that is already learned from elsewhere: 'It shall belong to the priest who offers it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer, קרבנות, and pushes it away. That law is already taught by a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״לכהן המקריב אותה לו תהיה״ already teaches that whoever takes part in offering a קרבן gets to eat from it. On the רגל all the shifts serve, so they would share the קרבנות anyway. If ״חלק כחלק״ only taught that, it would be extra, so it must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
It is derived from there, meaning it is already known from another source
The one who offers the sacrifice

phrases.english: If you say it means offerings,
that is derived from there:
'It shall belong to the priest who offers it'!
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק in ויקרא ז:ט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question in Step 2.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק would be extra, since sharing קרבנות is already taught by ״לכהן המקריב אותה לו תהיה״.

steps.title: It means the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the shared eating refers to the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the showbread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer: the eating that all shifts share equally is the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לחם הפנים eaten on this שבת was baked and placed the week before. The current shifts did no service for it, so the rule of ״המקריב״ would not give them a share. That is why a special פסוק is needed to say all the shifts share it equally on the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread, twelve loaves on the שולחן, replaced every שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why ״חלק כחלק״ is not extra. It covers food the priests did not themselves offer.

phrases.english: Rather: the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after Step 3 rejected קרבנות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The equal eating refers to the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Offerings unrelated to the festival stay with the shift of the week
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the sharing. קרבנות that are brought on the רגל but are not because of the רגל belong only to the משמר whose week it is, learned from ״לבד ממכריו על האבות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the shifts share equally even in obligations that come on the festival but not because of the festival. The verse says: 'Besides his sales by the fathers.' What did the fathers sell each other? 'I serve in my week, and you serve in your week.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe every קרבן brought on the רגל is shared by all the shifts. It then uses a פסוק to show that this is not so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people bring נדרים and נדבות while they are in ירושלים for the רגל, even though these have nothing to do with the רגל. The phrase ״ממכריו על האבות״ points to an old arrangement among the ancestors of the shifts: each shift owns its own week. So these offerings go only to the shift whose week it is, and only the festival offerings and the לחם הפנים are shared.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possible but wrong assumption)
The arrangements (sales) made by the forefathers

steps.confusionAlert: ״ממכריו״ is not about selling objects. It refers to the agreement between the founding fathers of the משמרות about whose week is whose.
steps.whatToRemember: On a רגל, all משמרות share the festival offerings and the לחם הפנים. Offerings not connected to the רגל stay with the shift of that week.

phrases.english: One might think even with obligations that come
not because of the festival, but on the festival,
the verse states:
'Besides his sales by the fathers' —
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק in דברים יח:ח.

phrases.english: what did the fathers sell to each other?
I serve in my week, and you in your week.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף בְּחוֹבוֹת הַבָּאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא מֵחֲמַת הָרֶגֶל בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and limits the equal-sharing rule of Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings brought on the רגל that are not due to the רגל belong only to the משמר whose week it is.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that on שבועות the distributor says to each כהן, 'Here is for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבועות he says to him, 'Here you go,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to move on to it. This is a setup line that opens the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שבועות falls on שבת, each כהן gets מצה from the לחם הפנים and חמץ from the שתי הלחם. The words ״וכו׳״ mean the rest of the משנה's line is assumed. Right after this quote, the גמרא introduces a separate dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the משנה uses for שבועות
And so on (the rest of the quoted line)

phrases.english: On Shavuot he says to him, 'Here you go,' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבועות that falls on שבת, the distributor hands each כהן מצה and חמץ together.

steps.title: Dispute: which ברכה comes first, סוכה or זמן?
steps.stepSummary: רב says to say the ברכה of סוכה first and then זמן (שהחיינו). רבה בר בר חנה says זמן first and then סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said, first the ברכה of סוכה, then the ברכה of זמן. רבה בר בר חנה said, first the ברכה of זמן, then סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two אמוראים. On the first night of סוכות, which ברכה do we say first: ״לישב בסוכה״ or ״שהחיינו״?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ברכות to say at the same moment, and the question is their order. רב puts סוכה first, and רבה בר בר חנה puts זמן first. The reasons are given in the next two steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Here ״סוכה״ and ״זמן״ are names of ברכות, not the סוכה hut itself or 'time' in general.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: סוּכָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְמַן.
phrases.english: Rav said: sukkah, and afterward time.
Rabba bar bar Hana said:
time, and afterward sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב אָמַר: סוּכָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the order of ברכות after the משנה quote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: סוכה then זמן. רבה בר בר חנה: זמן then סוכה.

steps.title: רב's reason: the מצוה of the day comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב puts סוכה first because the obligation that belongs to this day takes priority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said sukkah and then time, because the obligation of the day is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב says the ברכה of סוכה first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the סוכה is the special מצוה of this יום טוב, so its ברכה goes first. ״שהחיינו״ is not tied to this מצוה in the same way, so it comes after.
steps.whyThisMatters: The practical הלכה, as recorded in the שולחן ערוך, follows רב's order: ״לישב בסוכה״ first, then ״שהחיינו״.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: סוּכָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ זְמַן —
phrases.english: Rav said: sukkah and afterward time —
the obligation of the day takes priority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב's position in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה of the day's specific obligation (סוכה) comes before זמן.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה's reason: the more frequent comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה puts זמן first based on the rule ״תדיר ושאינו תדיר, תדיר קודם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said time and then sukkah, because when something frequent and something infrequent come together, the frequent one goes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה בר בר חנה says ״שהחיינו״ first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״שהחיינו״ is said on every יום טוב, while ״לישב בסוכה״ belongs only to סוכות, so זמן is the more frequent ברכה. The general rule of תדיר says the more frequent one goes first. The dispute is a clash between two ordering rules: the day's obligation versus frequency.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the day's obligation (סוכה) first. רבה בר בר חנה: the more frequent ברכה (זמן) first, by the rule of תדיר.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Hana said:
time and afterward sukkah —
between frequent and infrequent,
the frequent comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבה בר בר חנה's position, parallel to Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The more frequent ברכה (זמן) comes before the less frequent one (סוכה).

steps.title: Is this an older argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and רבה בר בר חנה are arguing about the same point as בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב and רבה בר בר חנה are arguing about the same thing that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possibility: maybe this argument already exists between בית שמאי and בית הלל. This line sets up the source it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often checks whether a later argument between אמוראים matches an earlier argument between תנאים. If it does, each אמורא would simply be following one side. The next steps bring the source and then test this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַב וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav and Rabba bar bar Chana

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: are arguing about the argument of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument from steps 7-9 and asks whether an older argument between תנאים is behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רב and רבה בר בר חנה the same as the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל?

steps.title: The ברייתא about the order of קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי say the ברכה on the day comes before the ברכה on the wine, and בית הלל say the wine comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: These are the matters that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about at a meal. בית שמאי say you first bless the day and then bless the wine. בית הלל say you first bless the wine and then bless the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the suggestion it just made. In קידוש, בית שמאי put the day first and בית הלל put the wine first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the structure of our case: two ברכות said one after the other, and an argument about which goes first. The ברכה on the day is like the main obligation of the day. The ברכה on the wine is a common, frequent ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: he blesses the day (the ברכה of קידוש)
he blesses the wine (בורא פרי הגפן)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה.
phrases.english: These are the matters between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding a meal.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: He blesses the day
and afterward blesses the wine.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: He blesses the wine
and afterward blesses the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בַּסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that step 10's suggestion is based on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the day, then the wine. בית הלל: the wine, then the day.

steps.title: The reasons of each side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains both sides. בית שמאי: the day is the reason the wine is brought, and the day became holy first. בית הלל: the wine makes קידוש possible, and also the wine ברכה is more frequent.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: bless the day first, then the wine, because the day is what causes the wine to be brought, and the day already became holy before the wine came. בית הלל say: bless the wine first, then the day, because the wine is what causes קידוש to be said. Another reason: the ברכה on wine is frequent and the ברכה on the day is not. When one thing is frequent and one is not, the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats both opinions, this time with their reasons. בית הלל give two separate reasons for putting the wine first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's logic matches רב (the obligation of the day comes first). בית הלל's second reason, תדיר קודם, is exactly the reason רבה בר בר חנה gave. But בית הלל also have a first reason: without wine, there would be no קידוש at all. That first reason becomes the key to רב's answer in step 14.
steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל have TWO reasons, not one. Keep them separate: (1) the wine makes קידוש happen, and (2) תדיר קודם. רב's answer in step 14 depends on that first reason.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: He blesses the day
and afterward blesses the wine,
because the day causes the wine to be brought;
and the day has already become holy
while the wine has not yet come.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: He blesses the wine
and afterward blesses the day,
because the wine causes the kiddush to be said.
Another explanation: the blessing over wine is frequent,
and the blessing over the day is not frequent.
Frequent and infrequent: the frequent comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא itself repeats the rulings from step 11 and adds the reasoning for each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the day comes first because it is the cause and it came first. בית הלל: the wine comes first because it makes קידוש happen, and also because תדיר קודם.

steps.title: Matching each אמורא to one side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out its suggestion: רב follows בית שמאי, and רבה בר בר חנה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב holds like בית שמאי, and רבה בר בר חנה holds like בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states its suggestion clearly. Each אמורא would be following one side of the old argument. This sets up the rejection that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason (the obligation of the day comes first) sounds like בית שמאי. רבה בר בר חנה's reason (תדיר קודם) is word-for-word בית הלל's second reason. The problem: if this were true, רב would be ruling against בית הלל, and the הלכה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav, who said it, holds like Beit Shammai,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה דְּאָמַר כְּבֵית הִלֵּל!
phrases.english: and Rabba bar bar Chana, who said it, holds like Beit Hillel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from steps 11-12 to רב and רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רב follows בית שמאי and רבה בר בר חנה follows בית הלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בית שמאי and בית הלל about the order of קידוש.

steps.title: רב can agree with בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that he can hold like בית הלל. Their main reason, that the wine makes קידוש happen, does not apply to סוכה and זמן, because we say the ברכה on the סוכה even without זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: I said my opinion even according to בית הלל. בית הלל only said the wine goes first there because the wine is what makes קידוש possible. But here, if there were no זמן, wouldn't we still say the ברכה on the סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב rejects the suggestion. He says his opinion does not conflict with בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says בית הלל's real reason is that wine is what makes קידוש possible: no wine, no קידוש. זמן does not work that way for סוכה. During the rest of the חג we say the ברכה on the סוכה without any זמן. So the reason for going first does not apply here, and רב can still put סוכה, the obligation of the day, first.

keyTerms.meaning: he can say to you (introduces a defense)
they only said their ruling (in that case)

steps.whatToRemember: רב is not limited to בית שמאי's view. בית הלל put wine first mainly because wine makes קידוש happen. The ברכה on the סוכה does not depend on זמן, so that reason does not apply, and רב can say סוכה first.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the הלכה follows בית הלל, showing that רב fits with בית הלל keeps רב's opinion a real option in practice.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
I said my view even according to Beit Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָתָם,
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only said their view there
because the wine causes the kiddush to be said;
but here, if there were no blessing of time,
would we not say the blessing of the sukkah?!
phrases.notes: During the rest of the חג we say the ברכה on the סוכה without זמן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 13's claim that רב must follow בית שמאי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument between רב and רבה בר בר חנה is the same as the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. It only shows that רב fits with בית הלל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores בית הלל's main reason, that wine makes קידוש possible. זמן does not make the ברכה on the סוכה possible.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה can agree even with בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: Just as רב showed he can fit with בית הלל, רבה בר בר חנה shows he can fit even with בית שמאי. So the two arguments are not the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה could tell you: I can say my view even according to בית שמאי. בית שמאי only said the day comes first in קידוש because the day is the reason the wine is brought. But here, even without a סוכה, wouldn't we still say זמן?
steps.whatsHappening: The other side now answers too. רבה בר בר חנה (who says זמן first) explains why בית שמאי's reason does not force him to put סוכה first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי put the day first because the wine only comes because of the day, so the wine depends on the day. Here, זמן does not depend on the סוכה at all, since we say זמן on the festival even without a סוכה. So בית שמאי's logic does not apply, and the suggestion from Step 10 is pushed off from both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: I can say my view even according to בית שמאי
They only said their view up to this point (only in that case)
The ברכה of שהחיינו, said for a new season or festival

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רבה בר בר חנה can fit with either side of the בית שמאי and בית הלל argument. So their dispute is NOT the same as the קידוש dispute.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana could say to you:
What I said holds even according to Beit Shammai.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai only said their view there (by kiddush)
because the day causes the wine to be brought;
but here, if there were no sukkah,
would we not still say the blessing of time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 14. רב pushed off the link from his side, and now רבה בר בר חנה pushes it off from his side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבה בר בר חנה must hold like בית הלל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית שמאי's reason (the day causes the wine) does not fit סוכה and זמן, because זמן is said even without a סוכה.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the שבועות bread distribution
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that on שבועות the כהן hands out the מצה (לחם הפנים) before the חמץ (שתי הלחם), even though the חמץ is the special obligation of the day. This seems to refute רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: on עצרת (שבועות) the כהן says, 'Here is מצה for you, here is חמץ for you.' Here the חמץ is the main item and the מצה is secondary, yet the משנה lists the מצה first. This is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to clearly go against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבועות, the חמץ loaves are the special offering of the day, and the מצה (the weekly לחם הפנים) is the regular, frequent item. The משנה still puts the frequent item first. That matches רבה בר בר חנה, who puts the frequent זמן first, and goes against רב, who puts סוכה (the special obligation of the day) first.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the מצה is the regular לחם הפנים, which is the 'frequent' item. It is NOT the מצה of פסח.

phrases.english: We learned: On Shavuot he says to him:
Here is matza for you, here is chametz for you.
But here, where the chametz is primary
and the matza is secondary, yet it teaches:
Here is matza and here is chametz,
a refutation of Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, בָּעֲצֶרֶת אוֹמֵר לוֹ: הֵילָךְ מַצָּה, הֵילָךְ חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the link to בית שמאי and בית הלל is pushed off, the גמרא attacks רב directly from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling: first סוכה, then זמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה puts the frequent item (מצה) before the special item of the day (חמץ). By the same logic, the frequent זמן should come before סוכה.

steps.title: רב: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a ברייתא shows אבא שאול holds that the חמץ comes first, so רב can follow אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could tell you: this is an argument between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: 'Here is מצה, here is חמץ.' But אבא שאול says: 'Here is חמץ, here is מצה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself by showing that the order in the משנה is not agreed on by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous view puts the frequent item first, but אבא שאול puts the main item of the day first. רב follows אבא שאול, so the משנה is no refutation of him. It only shows that רב sides with one תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument between תנאים

phrases.english: Rav could say to you: It is a dispute of tannaim.
As it is taught: Here is matza, here is chametz.
Abba Shaul says:
Here is chametz, here is matza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: רב follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was the only opinion, which would refute רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבא שאול puts the main item of the day first, and רב follows him.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא rules against רב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught publicly that the הלכה is not like רב. We say זמן first, then סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: not like the words of רב, who said סוכה and then זמן. Rather, זמן and then סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the practical ruling, starting with the opinion that rules against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer about proofs. It is a public teaching (דרש) of the practical הלכה, siding with רבה בר בר חנה's order.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly:
Not like the words of Rav, who said:
sukkah and afterwards time,
rather: time and afterwards sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth, the גמרא turns to the practical ruling.

steps.title: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rules like רב
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says the order is סוכה first, then זמן, like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת the son of רב אידי said: סוכה, and then זמן.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the opposite practical ruling and sides with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two practical opinions on the table. This sets up the גמרא's final decision in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi said:
sukkah and afterwards time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 18.

steps.title: Final ruling: סוכה first, then זמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules: first the ברכה of לישב בסוכה, then שהחיינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: סוכה, and then זמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final, binding decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows רב and רב ששת בריה דרב אידי. On the first night of סוכות in the סוכה, one says לישב בסוכה first, then שהחיינו.
steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: in קידוש on the first night of סוכות, say לישב בסוכה and then שהחיינו, like רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the order used in practice in קידוש on the first night of סוכות.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
sukkah and afterwards time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between Steps 18 and 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like רב: first סוכה, then זמן.

steps.title: What does 'other communal offerings' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier משנה and asks what the extra phrase 'ושאר קרבנות צבור' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the משמר whose time is scheduled [brings the offerings of the day], and also all other communal offerings. What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier משנה about which משמר brings the offerings on יום טוב. It asks what the extra words 'and other communal offerings' are meant to add. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed the תמידין and the other fixed offerings. So the extra phrase must be adding something that would not be obvious. The גמרא wants to know exactly which offerings these are.

keyTerms.meaning: A watch: one of the 24 rotating groups of כהנים, each serving one week
Whose time is scheduled: the watch whose regular week it is
Communal offerings, brought on behalf of all of כלל ישראל
What does this come to include?

phrases.english: The watch whose time is scheduled [etc.],
and the other communal offerings.
What does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the ברכות discussion to explaining the earlier משנה about the משמרות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra communal offerings are included by the words 'ושאר קרבנות צבור'

steps.title: It includes the communal sin-offerings for a mistaken ruling
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes פר העלם דבר של צבור and שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the bull brought for a communal error, and the goats brought for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'other communal offerings' adds the special קרבנות brought when the community sins because of a mistaken ruling of the סנהדרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings have no fixed date, so one might think they have no connection to the רגל. The משנה teaches that if they are brought during יום טוב, the scheduled משמר still brings them.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought when the community sins following a mistaken ruling of the סנהדרין
The goats brought for such a communal sin involving עבודה זרה

phrases.aramaic: לְאֵתוֹיֵי פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
phrases.english: To include the bull for a matter hidden from the community
and the goats for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes פר העלם דבר של צבור and שעירי עבודה זרה, even though they have no fixed time

steps.title: What does 'he brings everything' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ending of the משנה, 'והוא מקריב את הכל', adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it [the scheduled משמר] brings all of them. What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about a second extra phrase in the same משנה. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said 'other communal offerings'. So 'everything' must add yet another type of offering.

keyTerms.meaning: And it brings all of them

phrases.english: And it brings all of them.
What does this come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא מַקְרִיב אֶת הַכֹּל. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question, now asked about the next phrase of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is included by the word 'הכל'

steps.title: It includes the altar's 'dessert' offerings
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes קיץ המזבח, the extra עולות brought from communal funds when the מזבח would otherwise stand idle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the 'summer fruit' of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everything' includes קיץ המזבח. These were voluntary communal עולות brought so the מזבח would never stand empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיץ המזבח is compared to dessert, like summer fruit served at the end of a meal. These offerings are not tied to any day. Still, the משנה teaches that the scheduled משמר brings them, not the visiting משמרות.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar's 'summer fruit': communal עולות brought when the מזבח was otherwise empty

steps.whatToRemember: The scheduled משמר brings all offerings that are not specific to the רגל: the fixed ones, פר העלם דבר and שעירי עבודה זרה, and even קיץ המזבח.

phrases.english: To include the 'summer fruit' of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 and closes the explanation of the earlier משנה

steps.title: New משנה: when יום טוב is next to שבת, all watches share the bread equally
steps.stepSummary: If יום טוב falls right before or right after שבת, all the משמרות present share the לחם הפנים equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When יום טוב is next to שבת, whether right before it or right after it, all the משמרות were equal in sharing the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains how the 12 loaves of לחם הפנים, which are removed every שבת, are divided when the visiting משמרות of the רגל are also present on that שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the visiting משמרות stay through שבת for a good reason: they came early for יום טוב, or they could not leave before שבת. Because their presence is connected to the רגל, they get an equal share with the scheduled משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: The 12 showbread loaves, replaced each שבת and eaten by the כהנים

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A Festival that is adjacent to Shabbat,
whether before it or after it —
all the watches were equal
in the distribution of the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the related topic of dividing the לחם הפנים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום טוב is right next to שבת, all משמרות present share the לחם הפנים equally

steps.title: One day between יום טוב and שבת: 10 loaves and 2 loaves
steps.stepSummary: If one weekday separates יום טוב from שבת, the scheduled משמר takes 10 loaves and the delayed משמר takes 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there happened to be one day separating them, the scheduled משמר took 10 loaves and the משמר that was delayed took 2.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: one weekday separates יום טוב from שבת. Now the visiting משמר gets only a small share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one day in between, the visiting משמר could have left. However, it may not have had enough time to get home before שבת. Since its stay is only partly connected to the רגל, it receives just 2 loaves, and the scheduled משמר keeps 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who stays behind or is delayed

phrases.english: If one day happened to separate in between —

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁמָר שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ הָיָה נוֹטֵל עֶשֶׂר חַלּוֹת,
phrases.english: the watch whose time is scheduled would take ten loaves,
and the one that stayed behind takes two.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אֶחָד לְהַפְסִיק בֵּינָתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 25: a day in between reduces the visiting משמר's share
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scheduled משמר takes 10, delayed משמר takes 2

steps.title: Rest of the year: incoming and outgoing watches take 6 each
steps.stepSummary: On a regular שבת, when משמרות switch, the incoming and outgoing משמרות split the 12 loaves evenly, 6 and 6.
steps.simpleTranslation: And during the rest of the year, the incoming משמר takes six and the outgoing משמר takes six.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now describes a normal week with no יום טוב. On שבת one משמר finishes its week and the next one begins, so the loaves are divided between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משמרות serve in the בית המקדש on that שבת. The outgoing one does the מוסף service and the incoming one does the afternoon service. So the תנא קמא gives them an equal split.

keyTerms.meaning: The incoming משמר, starting its week
The outgoing משמר, finishing its week

phrases.english: And during the rest of the days of the year —
the incoming one takes six,
and the outgoing one takes six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יום טוב cases to the regular weekly case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normally the incoming and outgoing משמרות split the loaves 6 and 6

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the incoming watch gets 7, the outgoing gets 5
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees: the incoming משמר takes 7 loaves and the outgoing takes 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the incoming משמר takes seven, and the outgoing משמר takes five.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the previous opinion and gives the incoming משמר a larger share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that both משמרות share. He just gives the incoming one 2 extra loaves. (The גמרא will explain the reason for this extra share later.)
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not argue that the incoming משמר should get everything. He only changes the split from 6 and 6 to 7 and 5.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the incoming one takes seven,
and the outgoing one takes five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the 6 and 6 split of step 27
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incoming משמר takes 7 and the outgoing takes 5

steps.title: Incoming watch divides in the north, outgoing in the south
steps.stepSummary: The incoming משמר divides its loaves in the northern part of the עזרה, and the outgoing משמר in the southern part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incoming משמר divides [the loaves] in the north, and the outgoing ones in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where in the עזרה each משמר divides its loaves among its own כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The incoming משמר gets the north side. The north is the more important side, where the holiest קרבנות are slaughtered. This shows the incoming משמר is now the main משמר of the week.

phrases.english: The incoming ones divide in the north,
and the outgoing ones in the south.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the location of the division to the amounts already given
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incoming משמר divides in the north, outgoing in the south

steps.title: The penalty on משמר בילגה
steps.stepSummary: משמר בילגה always divides in the south, its ring is fixed in place, and its window is sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בילגה always divides in the south, and its ring is fixed, and its window is sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with an exception: one משמר, בילגה, was penalized and lost certain privileges permanently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when בילגה is the incoming משמר, it must divide in the less honored south. Its slaughtering ring is fixed so it cannot be used. Its storage niche for knives is sealed. These are public signs of disgrace, and the גמרא will explain the reason for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of one of the 24 משמרות
Its ring: floor rings used to hold animals during slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: The 12 loaves are split according to how connected each משמר is to that שבת: equally next to יום טוב, 10 and 2 with a day between, and 6 and 6 (or 7 and 5 according to רבי יהודה) normally. בילגה is the exception that always loses the honored north.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming גמרא, which explains why בילגה was penalized.

phrases.english: Bilga always divides in the south,
and its ring is fixed,
and its window is sealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the one exception to the north and south rule of step 29
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בילגה always divides in the south, its ring is fixed, and its niche is sealed

steps.title: What do 'before it' and 'after it' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by a יום טוב that comes 'before' or 'after' שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'before it,' and what is meant by 'after it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking a clarifying question about the משנה's wording: which יום טוב days count as 'before' שבת and 'after' שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that when יום טוב is next to שבת, whether before or after it, all the משמרות share the לחם הפנים equally. The words 'before' and 'after' are unclear: before or after what, and which festival day is meant? The גמרא wants to pin down the exact case.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'before it'
phrases.notes: This is about the משנה's case of a יום טוב right next to שבת.

phrases.english: and what is 'after it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its analysis of the משנה, whose rulings were laid out in the earlier steps.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific יום טוב days the משנה's 'before it' and 'after it' refer to.

steps.title: First reading rejected: that would just be שבת inside the festival
steps.stepSummary: Suggesting that 'before' is the first day of יום טוב and 'after' is the last day is rejected, because that is simply a שבת during the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'before it' means the first day of יום טוב and 'after it' means the last day of יום טוב, then that is the same as a שבת during the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible reading and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, שבת would fall between the first and last days of the festival, which means שבת falls inside the festival. That is not a separate case of 'יום טוב next to שבת.' It is just 'שבת inside the festival,' and the משנה would have called it that. So this reading cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, which introduces a suggestion that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'לפניה' as 'the festival day that comes first in the festival.' It means a יום טוב sitting just before שבת. In the correct reading that day is actually the LAST day of the festival.

phrases.english: If you say: 'before it' is the first festival day,
and 'after it' is the last festival day,
that is just a Shabbat within the festival.
phrases.notes: So this would not be a new, separate case

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 31 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading in which שבת falls between the first and last festival days
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the case the same as 'שבת inside the festival,' so the משנה's phrase would add nothing new.

steps.title: Correct reading: the festival's last day before שבת or its first day after שבת
steps.stepSummary: 'Before' means the last day of a festival falling just before שבת. 'After' means the first day of a festival falling just after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'before it' is the last day of יום טוב, and 'after it' is the first day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the festival ends on Friday and שבת follows right after. In the second case, שבת is immediately followed by the first day of a festival on Sunday. In both cases a holy day sits right next to שבת at the edge of the festival, not around it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which introduces the correct explanation

phrases.english: Rather: 'before it' is the last festival day.
phrases.notes: The festival ends right before שבת

phrases.english: 'After it' is the first festival day.
phrases.notes: The festival begins right after שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 32 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Before' means the last festival day just before שבת, and 'after' means the first festival day just after שבת.

steps.title: Why everyone shares: some came early and some stayed late
steps.stepSummary: Because the incoming משמר had to arrive early and the outgoing משמר had to stay late, the רבנן arranged for all of them to eat the לחם הפנים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since these came early and those stayed late, the רבנן set up a rule so that they would all eat together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the משנה's ruling that all the משמרות share equally in these cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the festival begins right after שבת, the incoming משמר cannot travel on שבת, so it must arrive before שבת, which is early. When the festival ends right before שבת, the outgoing משמר cannot leave on שבת, so it stays late. Since many משמרות end up in the בית המקדש on that שבת, the רבנן had them all share the bread as a group.
steps.whatToRemember: A יום טוב next to שבת means the festival's last day on Friday or its first day on Sunday. Because the משמרות are forced to come early or stay late, the רבנן had all of them share the לחם הפנים equally.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the equal sharing is a rabbinic arrangement. It responds to the practical fact that several משמרות are stuck in the בית המקדש together.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since these come early,
phrases.notes: The incoming משמר arrives before שבת

phrases.english: and these stay late,
phrases.notes: The outgoing משמר cannot leave on שבת

phrases.english: the Rabbis instituted a practice
so that they would eat together.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּהָנֵי מְקַדְּמִי וְהָנֵי מְאַחֲרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is defined, the גמרא gives the reason for the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משמרות are forced to come early or stay late, so the רבנן instituted that they all eat together.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה: 'If one day fell'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case, a single weekday between יום טוב and שבת, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If one day fell' between them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה to signal that it is moving on to analyze that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This refers to the משנה's ruling from step 26: when one weekday separates יום טוב and שבת, the scheduled משמר takes 10 loaves and the delayed משמר takes 2. Quoting it here opens a new discussion. It is not a new ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell, as when a date falls on a certain day
One day, here a single weekday in between

phrases.english: If one day fell (in between).
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא quotes the משנה to start the next topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of 'before it or after it' and turns to the משנה's next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case of one weekday between יום טוב and שבת: the scheduled משמר takes 10 loaves and the delayed משמר takes 2.
